summary: CausalSmith is an agentic pipeline for automated theoretical research in causal inference: it proposes results, solves them in natural language, stores them as a dependency graph, formalizes each node in Lean 4 against Causalean (a 8,179-declaration library built with LLM assistance), audits statement-to-claim match with an LLM, proves them, and writes papers. Over 144 recorded runs, 14 were accepted as sound, novel and fully Lean-proved; one closes a minimax gap from prior work.

claims.claim: 14 of 144 runs produced accepted, fully machine-checked, novel results
claims.evidence: Table 5: 14 accepted, 59 downgraded, 71 failed. 'Novel at tier' is judged by the pipeline's own LLM review; §7 states research-quality ratings have no independent human validation.

claims.claim: Accepted proofs are sound (only standard Lean axioms, no sorry/admit/axiom)
claims.evidence: §6.3: #print axioms on headline theorems in a clean build plus source scan (Appendix H). Proof validity is genuinely machine-checked.

claims.claim: Statement audit ensures the Lean statement matches the informal claim
claims.evidence: §7 concedes the audit is an LLM task and the error rate is not estimated; §7's phrase 'guarantees' is overstated.

claims.claim: Library feedback loop grows Causalean with reusable lemmas

patterns.note: Lean 4 type checking replaces LLM refereeing for proof validity; axiom audit on accepted results (§6.3).
Motivated by LLM reviewers accepting fabricated papers; yet novelty and statement-match still rely on unvalidated LLM review (§7).
Self-improving loop: run record screens later proposals and proven lemmas are promoted back into the library; no controlled before/after measurement.
Claim dependency graph as persistent run record driving formalization and audit (§5.1).

methodology.sample: 144 recorded runs (nine legacy runs excluded); 14 accepted
methodology.baselines: None; no comparison with other autoformalization or research-agent systems
methodology.models: GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.6 Sol for mathematics and Lean; Claude Opus 4.7/4.8/5 for review and planning; GPT-5.6 Terra for mechanical stages; lineup changed mid-campaign
methodology.variance: None; single campaign with changing models
methodology.contamination_controls: Novelty judged by pipeline; no independent literature check reported beyond LLM review
methodology.languages: Lean 4 / mathematics; no software engineering code

standards.artifacts: Library, pipeline and run records at github.com/Jiyuan-Tan/CausalSmith plus companion site

biases.detail: Pipeline rates its own research quality and novelty; no human validation (§7).
Statement-match audit error rate not estimated (§7).
One flagship result examined in depth (§6.2).
No cost per run reported in the sections reviewed.

coi.affiliations: Jiyuan Tan, Vasilis Syrgkanis (affiliations not printed in extracted text)
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None; uses OpenAI and Anthropic models

verdict_reason: off-topic: automated mathematical research in causal inference via Lean, not software engineering; the evaluation is also self-rated with no baselines.
applicability: Does not transfer to a Java backend team. The only portable idea is architectural: separate a deterministic checker (here Lean; for the team, compilers, schema validators, contract tests) from LLM judgment, and keep a persisted claim-dependency record, but the team already gets this from build/test gates without any of this machinery.
